purpose: Defines what an error is, how to classify errors by recoverability, how to treat causes, and the criteria for adding new error-distinguishing values.
summary: Purpose: criteria for adding values that distinguish errors in any mechanism (exit codes, agent results, error cases, API codes)
Definition of an error as an event that stops processing from following the intended flow, independent of expectation
Non-errors: things that can be judged, such as a nonexistent file referenced by a finding
Classification into recoverable and unrecoverable (fatal) errors; classification can shift when recovery options run out
Recovery is not always retry; alternative routes, waiting, or asking the user are other means
Causes (bug, failure, user input or environment) are separate from the error event
Bugs must not occur at runtime and get no dedicated values or recovery routes; failure defenses are out of scope unless requested
Questions to ask before adding a new error value
Severity catalog of violation patterns (critical, major, minor)
tasks: Designing exit codes or return values that distinguish errors
Writing error cases in requirements documents
Designing error handling in scripts and agents
Deciding whether to add a new error value or category
Reviewing code or documents for error handling violations
Deciding whether to attempt recovery or stop and report
title: エラーの定義・分類・原因
